_doc: SALVAGE (scripts/town/salvage.gd, the sim part `salvage` of the town; scripts/render/salvage_marks.gd draws it): furniture and wrecks of CLEARED places can be stripped for scrap, for good, once each. EVERY NUMBER OF IT IS HERE. kinds: the town's object kinds (the `kind` of data.objects: scripts/town/town_kit.gd KIT_PROPS and the streetscape's cars) that can be stripped, each {scrap: what it gives, seconds: how long the avatar's hands are at it (the crew's own timer reads the same number), name: the words of the prompt, stuff: what the rubble is (wood, metal, cloth: the pile the piece leaves)}. A kind that is not listed gives nothing and has no prompt (rugs, decals, chairs, lamps, boxes and crates, which are searched). THE PACE (RULES2, 2026-10-08, the owner: 'scraping cars takes 30 seconds, that is too long'): no piece takes more than 15 seconds of the avatar's hands (`seconds` times `seconds_mult`), and a car or a wreck takes about 10 (13.5 x 0.75 = 10.1 s, it was 44 and 40 x 0.75 = 33 and 30 s) for the same 4 scrap. The pieces that were over 15 s (beds, sofas, loveseats, the kitchen counter, the sink, the wardrobe, the fridge, the stove, the bathtub, the shed) are all 20 x 0.75 = 15 s now; the rest are as they were. What it adds up to (tools: the balance report of scripts/town/salvage.gd `potential` / `house_sum`, a 6-block town of seed 1): a house gives 11.5 scrap under its cap of 14 for 102 s of hands (it was 129 s, 11.2 s a scrap, now 8.9 s a scrap; about 2 minutes with the walking between its pieces), the pieces of the street 416 raw scrap (272 under the cell cap) for 1,300 s (it was 3,300 s: 8.0 s a scrap, now 3.1, and a car alone 2.5 s a scrap), so the street cap per 32 x 32 cell (3 cars) is what holds the street source down, not the hands. The first draft's three seconds a scrap made a house a minute's work, too fast a source against the fortifying. caps: house: the most scrap that all the furniture of ONE house can give (a house is 'picked clean' when it is reached; a piece that would go past it gives what is left); by_type: other caps by the house's `type` (residential, commercial, industrial, civic, farm, outbuilding); street_cell: the most scrap from the things standing in the street (cars, wrecks, sheds, benches) in one cell of cell_size tiles; cell_size. reach: how many tiles from the piece's edge the avatar stands (it must be inside the house for a piece in a house, and outside every house for one in the street). danger_r: a street piece cannot be stripped while one of the awake dead is within this many tiles of it. A house can be stripped only when it is CLEAR (`clearing.house_clear`, and none of the dead in it now), is not the base's (nor anything of the base's lot or compound), is not one of the houses the player is offered to claim until a base is claimed elsewhere, and the survivor who hides in a room has not joined yet (the pieces of that room are left). A searchable piece (a cupboard, a fridge...) can be stripped only after it has been searched. rubble: the colours of the pile a piece leaves (fill: the pieces', edge: their outline). sound: work_every the seconds between the sounds of the work, work_level and done_level the volumes. pop: seconds the '+3 scrap' is up. seconds_mult (TEMPO, 2026-10-07): a multiplier on every piece's seconds, hands and crew alike (0.75: about nine seconds of the hands for a scrap in a house, it was eleven; RULES2 shortened the longest pieces on top of it: `seconds` here are the raw numbers, the hands' time is `seconds` x `seconds_mult`).

cars._doc: LOOT IN THE STREET'S CARS (PH3 SCAV3, scripts/town/car_loot.gd): the parked cars and wrecks of the streets are CONTAINERS (id 'car<n>', n the place in the generator's object list: the same for a seed) that the avatar searches with E and the crew search on a scavenging trip. A car is searched once for good (the same `looted` flag as a cupboard: scripts/town/search.gd, saved), and a car cannot be stripped for scrap before it is searched (like a fridge). THE ROLL is made once per car from the town's seed, so a town always has the same cars with the same things in them. chance: by kind, the share of cars of that kind that hold anything at all (the rest are empty: the search says 'Empty'); a car that holds something has ONE item, and a second of another kind with probability `second` (at most two items). table: the items, w their weight, n [least, most] of the stock when it is found. search_s: seconds of a search (the container's `search_s`, times the run's tempo.search_mult like every container: the crew's timer reads the same number as the avatar's). reach: tiles from the car's edge the avatar stands to search it. trip: what the crew do on a scavenging trip (the Search-a-house order and the Scavenger job): after the house, the cars and wrecks within `radius` tiles of the house (of the first car, on a trip with no house) are searched nearest first and, when salvage allows it (the street cell cap, no awake dead within salvage `danger_r`), stripped for scrap too; `most` is the most cars one trip visits. How much it adds to the economy: a 6-block town has about 90 cars and wrecks and 20 to 30 of them hold something (seed 1: 26 of 90, 31 items, 64 units: 28 ammo, 15 food, 11 water, 9 scrap, 1 meds), against 13 units for an average house, so all the cars of a town together are about five houses of loot; the scrap of STRIPPING them (4 each, 12 under the cell cap) is the bigger source, as it was before. Lowering `chance` is the way to make the cars matter less.
